text:
Marina: Heads up — Legal asked for verifiable immutability proofs for our audit logs covering the last 2 years. They want tamper-evident receipts customers can present in audits, plus KMS key rotation history. Can we scope impact and a quick plan?

Kevin: Ack. Do we currently have production archive buckets with Object Lock (Compliance mode) enabled? :eyes:

Marina: Not fully. Dev buckets have Object Lock. Prod archive buckets have mixed settings — some retention but not sealed. No per-period signed manifests yet.

sre-bot: nightly-archive job finished 2026-03-18T02:14:00Z. backup_size=4.2TB; manifests_generated=false; last_kms_log_pull=2026-03-17T23:42:11Z

Ellen: High-level approach: (1) Make archive WORM-backed (S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode) or equivalent on-prem sealed store and add a legal-hold API. (2) Create per-period signed manifests + a hash-chain (chained manifests) to prove chain-of-custody. (3) Include KMS key metadata + rotation timestamps in each manifest and preserve CloudTrail/KMS audit entries alongside archives.

Sam: For customer-facing receipts: publish a signed bundle (manifest + signature) per export window. Customers verify signature with a published public key. Also expose a verification endpoint for auditors. +1 on hash-chain.

Kevin: Implementation notes: preserve KMS ARN and key version in manifest. Pull KMS rotation records from CloudTrail and store those events in our immutable audit-store. Need retention for CloudTrail events >= archive retention.

Marina: What are rough effort estimates? Need timeline for: enabling Object Lock on prod bucket(s) (org approvals), backfill existing archives with seals/proofs, KMS audit extraction, and a customer verification API.

Ellen: Estimates: prod Object Lock enable + approvals = 1 week (org/legal signoff needed). Backfill sealing (compute hashes, sign manifests, upload immutable copies, and switch pointers) = 2-3 weeks depending on throughput. KMS audit extraction scripting = 3 days + 2 days QA. Customer verify API + small UI = 2 weeks.

Kevin: Risks: enabling Object Lock on existing buckets is effectively irreversible. For backfill, we should avoid mutating current objects — instead upload sealed copies and update pointers/indices. Also ensure we don't break current restore flows.

Marina: Receipt/manifest format suggestion. We want minimal but verifiable fields. Proposed JSON manifest schema: start_ts, end_ts, objects: [{key, sha256, size}], kms_keys: [{key_arn, key_version, rotation_ts}], manifest_seq, prev_manifest_hash, signer_key_id, signature

Ellen: Example manifest snippet (short):

```json
{
  "start_ts": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "end_ts": "2024-03-31T23:59:59Z",
  "manifest_seq": 73,
  "prev_manifest_hash": "3f2b...ab9c",
  "objects": [
    { "key": "audit/2024/01/01/0001.log.gz", "sha256": "a3f5...9b2d", "size": 1048576 }
  ],
  "kms_keys": [
    { "key_arn": "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456:key/abcd-1234", "key_version": "v2", "rotation_ts": "2025-06-12T12:00:00Z" }
  ],
  "signer_key_id": "redwood-audit-signer-v1",
  "signature": "MEUCIQ..."
}
```

Kevin: For signing: use an HSM-backed signer (customer-facing public key published). Keep signer key rotation logs in the manifest chain. Hash algorithm: sha256. Use an atomic upload pattern for manifests + signature to avoid partial states.

Marina: Backfill approach idea: 1) list objects in archive window, 2) stream compute sha256 per object, 3) create manifest chunk, 4) sign + upload manifest to sealed bucket, 5) write index entry mapping window->manifest. We should parallelize by day/week to reduce runtime.

Ellen: Command we used for quick SHA check locally: `sha256sum audit-0001.log.gz | cut -d" " -f1` — script will be similar but streaming-friendly. Also plan to verify object integrity after copy by comparing hashes.

Sam: Customer-facing API: `/audit/verify?manifest_id=...` returns manifest JSON + signature + verification_status. We'll rate-limit and log queries. Consider caching verification results for a period.

Kevin: Compliance note: legal-hold requests must be honored even if retention would otherwise expire. Keep a per-customer legal-hold flag in manifest metadata and in retention policy engine.

Marina: Action items / owners: Ellen -> infra plan + prod Object Lock runbook + backfill design; Kevin -> KMS/CloudTrail extraction script and mapping to manifests; Sam -> API contract & verification UI; Marina -> coordinate legal approvals and update runbook.

Ellen: I'll draft the infra PR and a runbook for enabling Object Lock without accidental data loss. Will include rollback/alignment steps for pointers.

Kevin: I'll prototype KMS extraction today and post a short script.

Marina: Thanks — can everyone drop estimated PR/issue links here when created so Legal knows timeline? :+1:

sre-bot: created issue infra/5976: "object-lock-prod-enable-runbook" and job archive/backfill/2026-03 created.

Marina: Great. Keeping this open until we have approvals and the first signed backfill manifests.
